obligations.note: The base catalog bounds payments.privileged_idle_minutes to <= 15, but the change sets PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES in policy.py and the approved value in policy-params.json to 20. The control test passes only because it reads the edited policy-params.json value, not the obligation's bound.

No valid exception covers this deviation. EXC-0141 (SES-1) expired on 2026-09-06, before the 2026-10-06 review time. It covers only batch reconciliation service-account sessions on payments.session, and the change's author requested it.
Ticket CHG-26216 is standard and was approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-09-29, before the change opened. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover both touched paths.
The code_review approval is from sofia.santos, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author mara.costa (p-mcosta).
Both approvals name the head commit 60270cb, which is the change's only commit.

The CI run on head 60270cb succeeded: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. It includes the touched obligation's registered control test, test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy (exhaustive), which passed. That pass says nothing about the 15-minute bound, as noted under SES-1.
The touched components payments.policy and payments.controls-data are not marked security_sensitive in components.json, so no security_review is required.
The protected path controls/payments/policy-params.json changed. bao.tran, a control_owner in controls-office (outside the author's payments-eng team), approved the head commit.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not an emergency, so no PIR is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers policy.py or policy-params.json, so no earlier evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises the payments privileged idle timeout from 15 to 20 minutes, breaking SES-1's approved bound of <= 15 minutes. It edits the approved policy value along with the code, so the SES-1 control test still passes and does not show compliance. The only SES-1 exception (EXC-0141) is expired, limited to service-account sessions, and was requested by the author, so it cannot excuse the deviation. The process records (ticket, independent review, control-owner approval, CI on the final commit) are in order, but because SES-1 and EXC-1 are refuted the change must be rejected.
